**Finding: Compliant — no redline proposed.**

The IBM agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Bluefly:

- **§ 14.16 Freedom of Action** is affirmatively helpful and mutual: "Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others" — so we remain free to buy or build competing/alternative solutions.
- **§ 14.11 No Resale** ("Customer shall not resell the Services, in whole or in part") is a licence-scope limit on reselling IBM's own Services, not a restriction on our lines of business or on competing products, so it does not trigger the rule.
- **§ 13.2 (AUP)**, **§ 12.1 (License)**, **§ 14.17 (Limitation of Licenses)** and **§ 14.19 (Geographic Scope)** deal with acceptable use, licence scope and IBM's delivery footprint — none restrict what we may operate, procure or develop.
- Targeted searches for "compet", "exclusiv", "field of use", "territor", "engage in", "refrain from", "shall not develop" and "Customer shall not" surfaced no restrictive covenant binding us.

No fallback narrowing is needed, and there is no walk-away exposure (no post-term or undefined-scope restriction).
